datasets.measurement_observable: Orbital images of lunar surface and pit interiors used for morphology, off-nadir viewing, and stereo reconstruction
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Over mission timeline with varying lighting (not Sun-synchronous); authors note availability of ~10 years of NAC images for SCP and SWFP
datasets.location_coverage: Six reconstructed pits: Mare Tranquillitatis pit (MTP), Marius Hills pit (MHP), Mare Ingenii pit (MIP), Schlüter Crater pit (SCP), Southwest Mare Fecunditatis pit (SWFP), Lacus Mortis pit (LMP)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Pixel scales ranging from 0.26 to 2.2 m; nominal 0.5 m from 50 km altitude; up to ~2 m at ~200 km apoapse
datasets.pds_identifiers: PDS dataset: LRO-L-LROC-2-EDR-V1.0; DOI: 10.17189/1520250; PDS directory: http://pds.lroc.asu.edu/data/LRO-L-LROC-2-EDR-V1.0/
datasets.how_used: Primary image source for identifying pits, measuring pit geometry from off-nadir observations, manual/automatic stereo matching, and generating 3D point clouds of pit walls/floors (including roll-slew quantitative measurements).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: LRO MOON LROC 5 RDR V1.0 (NAC DTMs)
datasets.measurement_observable: Topography (DTMs) of pit surroundings (and limited pit floor sections) used as reference surfaces
datasets.location_coverage: NAC DTM coverage used for alignment/control at pits where available (explicitly noted for LMP, MHP, MIP, MTP); DTMs unavailable for SCP and SWFP in this study
datasets.spatial_resolution: High-resolution DTMs (exact post spacing not stated)
datasets.pds_identifiers: PDS dataset: LRO-L-LROC-5-RDR-V1.0; DOI: 10.17189/1520341; DTM directory (as cited): http://pds.lroc.asu.edu/data/LRO-L-LROC-5-RDR-V1.0/LROLRC_2001/DATA/SDP/NAC_DTM/
datasets.how_used: Used as updated SOCET SET-derived reference DTMs (“truth” surfaces) to align pit-wall stereo point clouds, provide alignment control points, and validate/verify reconstructed pit geometry.

datasets.location_coverage: Global lunar pit locations; used to provide the current list of known mare and highland pits summarized in Table 1
datasets.pds_identifiers: Product name in LROC PDS archive: SHAPEFILE_LUNAR_PIT_LOCATIONS; interactive catalog: http://lroc.sese.asu.edu/pits
datasets.how_used: Used as the published source of pit location details supporting the study’s pit inventory and geologic context assessment (mare/highland pit list and site selection context).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Apollo Panoramic Imager / Panoramic Camera photographs (Apollo 15 and 16)
datasets.measurement_observable: Photographic images used for multi-decadal change detection at pit sites
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: 1971 (Apollo 15) and 1972 (Apollo 16) compared to NAC images acquired 40+ years later
datasets.location_coverage: Mare Tranquillitatis pit (MTP) and Southwest Mare Fecunditatis pit (SWFP)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Allows identification of features ~5 m across (as stated)

datasets.how_used: Compared Apollo panoramic photographs with later LROC NAC images to assess whether pit rims/albedo streaking changed over ~40 years; no changes observed at the stated detection scale.

output_parsed.paper_title: Lunar Pit Morphology: Implications for Exploration

queries.query: For geometric control of pit-interior stereo reconstructions, I need a high-resolution LRO LROC Narrow Angle Camera stereo-derived digital terrain model (RDR-level) that covers the surroundings of the Compton mare pit on the Moon so I can register oblique wall point clouds to an external “truth” surface and quantify funnel-to-rim topography.

To assess approach-path hazards and traverse limits into a lunar mare pit, I need a LRO LROC Narrow Angle Camera DTM-derived slope product (RDR-level) for the Mare Ingenii pit area on the Moon, enabling quantitative mapping of steep funnel sectors versus more navigable slopes for mission planning.

queries.query: For the Moon, I need Apollo 15 orbital panoramic-camera support ephemeris (spacecraft position/attitude information) for the 1971 mission interval so I can rigorously co-register the historic panoramic photographs over a mare collapse-pit site in Mare Tranquillitatis with modern LRO NAC basemaps for multi-decadal (~5 m scale) rim-change and albedo-streak stability checks.

For the Moon, I need Apollo 16 orbital panoramic-camera support ephemeris (spacecraft position/attitude information) for the 1972 mission interval to geolocate and co-register the historic panoramic photographs over the southwest Mare Fecunditatis region with later high-resolution orbital imaging, enabling a multi-decadal assessment of pit-rim morphology and interior-shadow/albedo changes at approximately 5 m detectability.

final_output.query: Retrieve the PDS context definition for the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera so I can verify Narrow Angle Camera imaging characteristics (line-scan geometry and sub-meter to few-meter pixel scales) relevant to off-nadir stereo observations used in 3D reconstruction of lunar pit interiors.

Retrieve the PDS context record for the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter spacecraft platform to correctly associate LROC NAC raw imaging observations with the proper instrument host and mission configuration when analyzing off-nadir pit interior imaging and stereo geometry.

For geometric control of pit-interior stereo reconstructions, I need a high-resolution LRO LROC Narrow Angle Camera stereo-derived digital terrain model (RDR-level) that covers the surroundings of the Compton mare pit on the Moon so I can register oblique wall point clouds to an external “truth” surface and quantify funnel-to-rim topography.

To assess approach-path hazards and traverse limits into a lunar mare pit, I need a LRO LROC Narrow Angle Camera DTM-derived slope product (RDR-level) for the Mare Ingenii pit area on the Moon, enabling quantitative mapping of steep funnel sectors versus more navigable slopes for mission planning.

I need a global GIS catalog of lunar pit entrance locations (as a vector layer) suitable for screening candidate skylight-access points and linking each pit to its geomorphic setting (mare vs highland) on the Moon.

Provide a lunar-wide pit-location vector dataset (GIS shapefile-type catalog product) that can be used as the authoritative inventory for spatial statistics of pit distributions and for selecting sites for high-resolution LRO imaging follow-up and 3D pit-interior reconstruction.

For the Moon, I need Apollo 15 orbital panoramic-camera support ephemeris (spacecraft position/attitude information) for the 1971 mission interval so I can rigorously co-register the historic panoramic photographs over a mare collapse-pit site in Mare Tranquillitatis with modern LRO NAC basemaps for multi-decadal (~5 m scale) rim-change and albedo-streak stability checks.

For the Moon, I need Apollo 16 orbital panoramic-camera support ephemeris (spacecraft position/attitude information) for the 1972 mission interval to geolocate and co-register the historic panoramic photographs over the southwest Mare Fecunditatis region with later high-resolution orbital imaging, enabling a multi-decadal assessment of pit-rim morphology and interior-shadow/albedo changes at approximately 5 m detectability.
